source_definition.value: Individual cognitive reappraisal scores from the reappraisal subscale of the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (ERQ), which measures the habitual use of cognitive reappraisal; the ERQ items are rated from 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree).

model_settings.value: Subject-level general linear models in SPM5 included separate boxcar regressors for the two cue conditions and four target conditions, each convolved with the canonical HRF and its temporal and dispersion derivatives. Button presses convolved with the same basis functions and six head-motion parameters were included as nuisance regressors. Individual contrast maps were entered into whole-brain regression analyses with reappraisal scores as covariates; results were FDR corrected at p < .05.

Cued Emotional Conflict Task (CECT)

description.value: Participants responded to happy or sad facial expressions according to an actual or opposite cue.

spans.text: On each CECT trial, a preparatory cue instructs participants to respond to the actual emotion or to the opposite emotion of an upcoming stimulus.
actual

description.value: Participants were cued to attend to and name the actual emotion of the subsequently presented happy or sad facial expression by pressing the button labeled with that emotion; this condition required responding to the facial expression without reversing its emotional category.

spans.text: opposite

description.value: Participants were cued to attend to and name the opposite emotion of the subsequently presented happy or sad facial expression by pressing the button labeled with the other emotion; this condition required inhibiting the dominant response to the facial expression and selecting its opposite.

spans.text: The CECT was programmed in E-prime (Psychology Software Tools Inc, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania).
